newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy prosecutor seeks jail for ex-Publitalia boss.
newsitem.headline: Italy prosecutor seeks jail for ex-Publitalia boss.

text.p: An Italian magistrate called on Thursday for a five year jail sentence for the former boss of ex-prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Publitalia advertising group who is on trial on charges of false billing and tax fraud.
Magistrate Luigi Marini sought the sentence for Publitalia's former chairman, Marcello Dell'Utri.

The prosecution alleges that Publitalia and two of its subsidiaries, Publieuropa and Publiespana, created some nine billion lire of assets through inflated bills for sporting sponsorships which were not recorded in company books.
The cash was allegedly spent in various ways, including hand-outs to business associates.
Publitalia is part of the Mediaset empire controlled by Berlusconi. The media mogul told reporters attending Dell'Utri's trial last week that Publitalia's accounts were completely clean.

Dell'Utri has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Oreste Dominioni, has said the only person responsible for the affair was Gianpaolo Prandelli, former Publitalia deputy general manager, who accepted a reduced 18-month prison sentence under a plea-bargaining deal before the trial began.
